forecaster_note: Peaky NE swell — waist to chest high at most spots. Offshores this morning but pretty raw and junky, settling a little with time as they hold till mid-morning. Similar size through the day, then light southerlies come through: S corners and N-facing spots best this afternoon. Size grades up Sat with short-period NE wind wave. — Surfline forecaster (Fri 2 Oct)

wind.summary: Light WNW 5 kph offshore at dawn, cross-shore S by 9am, then ESE onshore 15 kph from noon (gusts ~18 by 6pm).

days.label: Today
days.note: Peaky NE wind swell (5.5ft @ 7s, ~304 kJ — fun, not powerful) with a tiny 0.8ft S swell. Light WNW offshore at dawn but the forecaster calls it raw and junky; winds go cross-shore ~9am then onshore ESE from noon, with light southerlies later. Best 6:30–9:30am. Low 5:22am, high 11:59am. Long Reef picks up the most size; Dee Why gets the NE at its best angle.

Minor S swell (dead-S angle, wraps poorly at Dee Why)

dee-why.window: Light WNW offshore at first light, cross-shore by 9am, onshore from noon. NE 47° is the ideal angle but it's raw and junky — go early, pick the cleaner peaks. Dead-S component is tiny.

tip.label: NE peaks — frontside at the Point
tip.text: Short-period NE is the good angle at Dee Why. Frontside rights at the Point, backside lefts on the beach peaks. 7s means punchy not powerful — commit and stay on the drive.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE wind swell — the good angle

long-reef.window: Picks up the most size of the four and rates best (fair). Offshore at dawn, cross-shore by 9am, onshore from noon. Reef handles the minor S better than the beachies.

tip.label: Frontside rights off the reef
tip.text: Waist to shoulder. 7s wind swell can back off between sets — be patient and position on the peak that lines up.

swells.label: Dominant short-period NE wind swell — the good angle
Minor S swell (dead-S angle, wraps poorly at Dee Why)

curl-curl.window: Light offshore early, then cross-shore/onshore. Fun and peaky when it cleans up; find the bank with the best shape.

tip.label: Find the bank
tip.text: Smaller and peaky — look for the peak holding its shape and take the shoulder. Flowy session board.

manly.window: Offshore/cross at dawn, onshore ESE from noon. Smallest of the four — mostly worth it for an easy one.

tip.label: Sheltered fallback
tip.text: Smaller and softer. Only worth it if the others are too raw.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Size grades up with short-period NE wind wave — chest to maybe head high and peaky at most breaks. Light trending breezy N/NE; mornings and north corners cleanest, biggest in the arvo but with lighter morning winds. Mid-morning is workable. Sizes estimated from forecaster text.

dee-why.window: Light morning winds trending breezy N/NE — NE 40–50° swell is the good angle here. Go 8–11am for the cleanest window; north corner best.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sat: size grading up, peaky chest–head NE wind wave, N/NE breeze — go early. Sun: winds swing favourable and clean up an easing E/NE short-period swell, maybe some local S — fun to good peaky surf, but forecaster says it's uncertain so recheck. Daylight saving starts Sun 4 Oct (clocks +1h). Mon looks like a nice-sized peaky S + E/NE mix as the coastal low moves away.
